architecture_decisions: 5.1 Structural success and acceptance verification are separate facts
validations: AC-01: validate protected requirement — Tests and authoritative records identify the exact existing behavior: the static-web validator is structural, while autonomy currently stamps the complete acceptance map into TEST/VERIFY `acceptance_ids_verified`.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — A production-shaped PLAN-bound static-web run with successful TEST records scope `STRUCTURAL_ONLY`, all protected IDs as targeted/unverified, and an empty verified list.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — The same exact evidence partition is required for successful VERIFY.
AC-04: validate protected requirement — Tests prove missing, malformed, partial, drifted or non-static PLAN execution-contract identity cannot authorize the structural-only envelope.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Tests prove a non-static run or direct protected-stage call that supplies `STRUCTURAL_ONLY` / `static-web-v1` fields without an exact resolved static-web PLAN identity fails closed.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — Tests reject duplicate, omitted, added or overlapping verified/unverified/targeted IDs and reject any scope value other than the fixed server value.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Existing full-verification paths continue to require `acceptance_ids_verified` to exactly match the protected acceptance map and existing regressions remain green.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — A fully successful structural static-web BUILD/TEST/VERIFY sequence reaches REVIEW, not FAILED or COMPLETE, with explicit unverified acceptance evidence and the existing REVIEW-required event/stop semantics.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Existing review validation still requires recommendation PASS, exact all acceptance IDs verified and the current implementation workspace digest. Structural TEST/VERIFY evidence alone cannot complete REVIEW.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Run evidence projection/event metadata safely exposes structural scope and verified/unverified counts/IDs where allowed, while existing secret/private-reasoning guards remain intact.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Diff review proves no command, validation profile, execution-contract digest, provider/model/credential/network, source-lineage, Git/Preview, merge, retry, lifecycle, REVIEW-completion or production authority increase.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Spec validation, authentic DSPy SpecCritic/SpecCompiler, strict DSPy plan validation, focused tests, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, Workstream Spec Validation and P2 CI pass on exact reviewed heads.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — Exact merged source reaches production READY; normal production preflights pass; canonical `/health` and `/ready` return HTTP 200; exact-deployment runtime scans are clean.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — After deployment, a safe new static-web run or bounded production-shaped replay proves successful structural TEST/VERIFY no longer records every acceptance criterion as verified and still stops at human REVIEW.

critique: The current implementation of the `static-web-v1` application does not meet the requirements outlined in the brief. Specifically, the evidence for structural acceptance is not truthful, and the verification process does not ensure that the static-web command completed successfully against the exact accepted source lineage. The current implementation may still progress to the existing REVIEW boundary because REVIEW is already the human completion authority, but protected execution must not claim behavioral proof it did not produce.
